correctness.rationale: For a contraction T with Tx=y, B intersect T inverse of the minimal face of y is a face containing x; injectivity gives d(x)≤d(y). Conversely, choose norm-one functionals exposing the two minimal faces and an isomorphism between their (n−1)-dimensional kernels embedding the k-dimensional tangent span of the source face in the l-dimensional target tangent span. The explicit T_epsilon(z)=f(z)y+epsilon U(z−f(z)x) is invertible since g∘T=f and U is bijective. A sufficiently small common epsilon maps every ball vertex into B: source-face vertices enter the target face by relative interior, opposite-face vertices by symmetry, and all other vertices by strict interior margins. Finiteness of vertices proves contraction for every n≥1. Exact rational tests on 12 vertices in six ordered face-rank cases independently pass, without substituting numerical evidence for the general proof.

value.rationale: Contractive-automorphism reachability is a motivated natural invariant of Banach unit spheres. The result completely classifies this preorder for the entire real-polyhedral class by one intrinsic facial dimension, regardless of combinatorial complexity, and resolves intermediate ranks in dimensions at least three, beyond earlier planar and top-face theorems. It yields a uniform n-stratum structure through an invertible, globally contracting construction. The independently known dense-orbit corollary is identified as such rather than counted as novel value.
